question: How much will Nasdaq-100 Futures total price returns exceed S&P 500 Futures in these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 21 - Oct 2)

calls.reasoning: Reference class: all 10-trading-day windows of NDX minus SPX price return, 2015-2026; drift is small and positive (~+5pp/yr long-run, and 2026 YTD +17.0% vs +12.7-12.9% through Sep 4 = ~+0.25pp per biweekly window), dispersion dominates the mean by ~6x. Window Sep 21-Oct 2 is 10 sessions, none elapsed as of Now. Futures-vs-index carry differences (NQ ~0.6% div yield, ES ~1.2%, single Dec contract post-Sep-18 roll) shift the spread by only ~0.02pp - immaterial. Two-sided case: for NDX, AI earnings breadth (>half of NDX Q2 EPS +20% y/y), Nvidia's FY28 +70% guide, semis +60% YTD, Micron reporting in-window; against NDX, a ~83%-priced Sep 16 hike with the 10y at 4.97% (duration hit lands hardest on high-multiple names), Brent ~$95 helping SPX energy where NDX has none, quarter-end rebalancing out of 2026 winners, and Russell 2000 +20.2% YTD showing the rotation is broadening beyond mega-cap tech. These roughly offset, so I stay near the base-rate drift: median +0.25pp, EV slightly lower for mild negative skew (macro-driven drawdowns hit NDX at ~1.2 beta). Escape mass: an AI-multiple unwind on a 5% 10y (2022-Jan and 2024-Jul precedents both produced ~-5pp two-week spreads) prices 2% below -5; a dovish-surprise or chip-news melt-up prices 1.5% above +5. Evidence is moderately thin and partly conflicting (one Sep-10 piece calls NDX a 2026 laggard stuck in a range while three others document clear YTD outperformance), which is a further reason to sit near the reference class rather than lean. Most sources were read via search-result summaries; only the EBC piece was opened in full.

SUBJECT: NDX-100 futures minus S&P 500 futures price return, window Sep 21 2026 -> Oct 2 2026 20:00 UTC (10 trading sessions). Units: percentage points. Bounds -5/+5, both open.

EVENT WINDOW: Sep 21 2026 -> Oct 2 2026 20:00 UTC per the criteria; as of Now (2026-09-14T17:27Z) 0% elapsed - the window has not begun and starts in ~7 days.

RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off FUTURES price returns (NQ vs ES), not cash-index or total-return-with-dividends. Sep 18 2026 is quad-witching, so the entire window sits in a single December contract with no roll inside it. Carry math: NQ dividend yield ~0.6%/yr vs ES ~1.2%/yr against a ~3.5-3.75% funding rate makes the futures spread differ from the cash-index spread by ~0.02pp over 14 calendar days.

STATUS QUO: the two indices track each other closely; a 10-session window with no regime break produces a small spread near the year's average daily drift, not a large one.

BASE RATES
- Over ALL overlapping 10-trading-day windows 2015-2026: NDX-SPX mean/median ~+0.25 to +0.3pp; SD ~1.3-2.0pp depending on vol regime (dispersion exceeds the mean by roughly 6x).
- CONDITIONAL on 2026 YTD pace: NDX +17.0% vs SPX +12.7-12.9% through Sep 4 (EBC/ebc.com Sep 2026; Motley Fool Sep 9 2026) = +4.1-4.3pp over ~170 sessions, i.e. ~+0.25pp per 10 sessions.
- CONDITIONAL on high-vol/macro-shock windows (2022 rate shock, Jul 2024 unwind, Apr 2025): two-week spreads of -4 to -5pp have occurred; such windows are a small minority of the 2015-2026 sample.
- CONDITIONAL on current implied vol (VIX 17.84 close Sep 11 2026, a 28-session high; NDX vol runs ~1.2x SPX; daily NDX/SPX correlation ~0.97): implied 10-day spread SD ~1.2-1.4pp before allowing for rotation autocorrelation.

EVIDENCE - supports NDX side
- Nvidia (8.83% of NDX) Q2 report Aug 26 2026: beat, guided FY2028 revenue growth ~70% vs ~44% consensus; stock +7.4% to +8.7% (CNBC, Aug 26 2026).
- Over half of Nasdaq-100 companies posted >=20% y/y Q2 EPS growth, described as the broadest in 4.5 years (EBC, Sep 2026).
- PHLX Semiconductor Index ~+60% YTD as of Sep 3 2026, with underlying earnings up >60% (EBC).
- NDX has outperformed SPX in 2026 despite the 10y real yield rising from 1.93% to 2.42% and nominal from 4.18% to 4.77% (EBC, Sep 3 2026 data) - the rate headwind has not historically stopped it this year.
- Micron (4.77% of NDX) and AMD (3.28%) are large 2026 contributors; Micron reports inside the window (late September, fiscal Q4).

EVIDENCE - supports SPX side
- Fed: rates held at 3.50-3.75% in July on a 9-3 vote with three dissents FOR a hike; after Warsh's Jackson Hole speech, market-implied odds of a 25bp HIKE on Sep 16 2026 moved from ~30% to ~56% (CNBC Aug 28) and are quoted ~83% in early-September coverage. RBC now forecasts three hikes by year-end vs zero previously; fed funds futures imply ~50% odds of 4.00-4.25% by December (UDN, Sep 12 2026).
- 10y Treasury closed 4.974% on Sep 11 2026, near 5% for the first time in three years; commentary flags 5% yields plus $100 oil as the specific combination that would pressure AI/chip leadership (UDN Sep 12 2026).
- Brent ~$95.63, WTI ~$91.01 amid US-Iran tension (Sunday Guardian, Sep 13 2026). Energy is ~4% of the S&P 500 and ~0% of the Nasdaq-100.
- Russell 2000 +20.2% YTD, ahead of both NDX and SPX - the 2026 leadership is broader than mega-cap tech (Motley Fool, Sep 9 2026).
- At least one Sep 2026 piece characterizes NDX as range-bound and a 2026 laggard on AI-valuation and AI-economic-impact concerns (Motley Fool, Mar 10 2026 piece updated framing) - this conflicts with the YTD numbers above and is flagged as contested, not settled.
- Quarter-end (Sep 30) falls inside the window: mechanical rebalancing tends to trim the year's winners.

CALENDAR INSIDE OR ADJACENT TO THE WINDOW
- FOMC decision Sep 16 2026 - five days BEFORE the window opens; only its aftermath (guidance, yield path) is in-window.
- Quad witching Sep 18 2026 - before the window; contract roll completed.
- Micron fiscal Q4 earnings, late September; Costco early October - both NDX members.
- August PCE inflation print, late September.
- September employment report, Friday Oct 2, 08:30 ET - lands INSIDE the final session, before the 20:00 UTC resolution.
- Government funding: CR signed Sep 2 2026 funds agencies through Dec 11 2026 (The Hill; NBC News) - no Oct 1 shutdown risk in this window.

MARKET CHECK: no prediction-market contract found on NDX-vs-SPX relative return at any horizon. Kalshi lists Nasdaq-100 absolute level ranges and Fed-decision markets; Polymarket and Manifold title searches returned no candidate. Treat as 'no market anchor'.

RECENT LEVELS (for orientation, not extrapolation): Sep 11 2026 close S&P 500 7,656.98 (+0.9% on the day), Nasdaq Composite 26,333.04 (+1.0%); for the week Sep 7-11 S&P -0.8%, Nasdaq -0.7%, Dow -1.6% (AP via Washington Post, Sep 11 2026). August CPI: core +0.3% m/m, headline +3.4% y/y.

SEARCHED FOR BUT NOT FOUND: (a) any direct time series or published statistic of the NDX-minus-SPX spread over 10-trading-day windows - no downloadable price data was reachable from this environment, so the dispersion figures above are reconstructed from implied vols and the vol/correlation relationship rather than measured; (b) VXN (Nasdaq-100 volatility index) level for September 2026; (c) any news dated after Sep 13 2026; (d) analyst previews specific to the Sep 21-Oct 2 stretch; (e) Micron's exact fiscal-Q4 report date.

I keep the median just below that drift (+0.20) because the regime cuts both ways: a Fed hike expected Sep 16 with the 10y near 5% and the real 10y up 49bp YTD is a duration headwind for the higher-multiple index, and the AI trade was being rattled on Sep 14 (OpenAI IPO delay, safety-related appeals), while Nvidia's blowout guidance, >20% Q2 EPS growth at over half of NDX names and ~60% YTD semis earnings growth push the other way. calls.reference_class: All 10-trading-day windows of Nasdaq-100 minus S&P 500 front-month futures price return, 2015-2026 (two-week relative-return differences)

calls.reasoning: Reference class: 10-trading-day NDX-minus-SPX price-return spreads, which are roughly symmetric with a mean near the structural NDX drift (~+4-5%/yr, i.e. ~+0.18pp per two weeks) and fat tails. 2026 shows that drift is not reliable: NDX led massively in May (+10.6 vs +5.3), fell behind by late July (7.8% vs 9.0% YTD TR), then led again in the August AI re-ignition; trailing-12m QQQ +21.99% vs SPY +17.28%. I shade the median down from the long-run drift to roughly zero because the live macro setup is the historically worst one for NDX relative performance - a hiking Fed (Sep 16 FOMC, core CPI 3.4%, RBC now at three hikes), 10y at 4.97%, Brent ~$95 favoring energy which is absent from NDX - compounded by the Sep 14 AI-safety shock (NQ -1.72% vs ES -0.70%). Offsetting: AI capex/earnings momentum (Nvidia's 70% growth projection) has repeatedly re-ignited the trade within weeks. The window is clean of the largest scheduled catalysts (FOMC is Sep 16, before it; the Oct 1 shutdown was averted by the Sep 2 CR through Dec 11); it does contain Micron earnings (~Sep 23), quarter-end rebalancing, PCE, and the Oct 2 payrolls print - vol-raising, direction-neutral. Dispersion is the main call: VXN/VIX at 22.3/15.8 is a wide gap, implying ~1.6pp SD over 10 sessions, so I keep a 4.1pp 10-90 width rather than the narrower band a calm-regime prior would give. Slight left skew because NDX beta >1 combines with equity markets' own negative skew. Escape mass is small but real: ~1.5% below -5 (AI-safety regulatory shock, yields through 5.25%, a mega-cap duration crush) and ~1.0% above +5 (an August-style AI melt-up or dovish surprise). No human prediction market prices this spread, so no crowd anchor.

calls.reconciliation: In dispute: (a) the QQQ/SPY +4.1pp YTD gap vs Motley Fool's late-July Composite +7.8% vs S&P +9.0% — resolved as not contradictory (Composite is not NDX-100, the dates differ by six weeks, and the August AI re-ignition bridges them), so the ~+0.2pp/10-session drift anchor holds; (b) VIX on Sep 11 quoted as 17.84 by Run 1 vs 15.84 by Runs 2 and 3 — two-of-three plus Run 3's paired VXN datum favour 15.84, and it is immaterial since VXN 22.3 drives the spread vol; (c) Barclays' claim that Mag7 ex-Tesla underperformed the S&P for 92% of YTD alongside NDX leading YTD — reconcilable only if the lead is semi-driven (SOX ~+60% YTD), which is plausible but NOT settleable from the dossiers with no web access this run, so I let it cap confidence in the drift rather than resolve it either way. Pure judgment, no evidence breaking the tie: whether the Sep 14 AI-safety session (NQ -1.72% vs ES -0.70%) should persist seven sessions into the window. I would bet it does not — it is narrative-level with no earnings mechanism — so I do not shade to Run 3's +0.05, but I also do not take the full +0.24 drift given the Barclays tension: +0.15. Dispersion is carried forward from Run 3's implied-vol computation, which I recomputed independently (VXN/VIX at 0.95-0.97 correlation gives 1.6-1.75pp SD over 10 sessions) and set at the upper-middle, 4.35pp, because all three runs' in-window catalyst list is vol-raising. Escape masses sit between the runs' values: precedents for -4 to -5pp two-week spreads exist (2022, Jul 2024, Apr 2025) and require ~3 SD here, so 1.8% below and 1.2% above under fat tails. disagreements.verdict: Unanimous across all three runs and internally consistent; accepted.

disagreements.claim: No prediction market or bookmaker prices the NDX-minus-SPX relative return
disagreements.verdict: Three independent checks (Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi) all returned none found; Kalshi's contracts are absolute-level, different horizon, not a near-miss worth anchoring on. No crowd anchor.

disagreements.claim: The Sep 14 AI-safety selloff should shade the median toward zero (Run 3, +0.05) vs be discounted (Runs 1-2, +0.20/+0.25)
disagreements.verdict: No evidence breaks this. I take the reading I would bet on: a one-day narrative move seven sessions before the window opens, with no earnings mechanism, decays. Median set at +0.15.

disagreements.claim: A hiking Fed with the 10y near 5% is a live duration headwind for the higher-multiple index
disagreements.verdict: Weighted down: the dossiers show the real 10y rose 49bp YTD 2026 while NDX led by ~4pp, and the Sep 16 hike resolves before the window opens. Real but largely priced.
Recomputed independently: VXN 22.3 / VIX 15.8 at correlation 0.95-0.97 implies 1.6-1.75pp SD over 10 sessions, i.e. 4.1-4.5pp. Set at 4.35, the upper-middle, for the in-window catalyst stack.
